compiled_state.description:
## Context
The hardening byte-equivalence test executes both production `_convert` and a copied `_legacy_convert` for all 884 prepared corpus units. The copied oracle shares conversion constants with production; changing `_PANDOC_TO` to `plain` made both sides agree, demonstrating coupling. Combined corpus+hardening invokes Pandoc 3,421 times under xdist; the legacy half adds 884 subprocesses. Immutable expected outputs detect 799/884 of that mutation while production `_convert` still invokes the real pinned Pandoc for every unit. This preserves ADR 0095 because every conversion assertion continues to cross the real production binary. Golden fixtures match Pandoc, Kubernetes, and Rust practice. No prior rejection was found; `dimmed-supersweet-xenarthra` defers production spawn redesign, not independent test oracles.

## Plan
- Inventory the 884 prepared corpus inputs and pin their ordering/cardinality.
- Produce an immutable legacy-output fixture containing generator Pandoc version and SHA-256 binary fingerprint. Add a deterministic regeneration command/script and a fast installed-version drift assertion.
- Replace only the copied `_legacy_convert` subprocess call with lookup of the immutable output. Continue to invoke production `_convert` with real Pandoc for every prepared unit on every per-change run.
- Strengthen the oracle so a production format mutation fails against the independent expected output; preserve timeout/group-reap tests unchanged.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, the `_PANDOC_TO=plain` defect-seeded mutation, full focused corpus/hardening suites, gates, and paired timing. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring live legacy subprocess comparisons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 884 prepared corpus units still pass through production `_convert` and real Pandoc in per-change CI.
- [ ] The copied legacy Pandoc subprocess implementation is removed from the byte-equivalence oracle and replaced by immutable expected output.
- [ ] Fixture metadata records the exact generating Pandoc version and SHA-256 fingerprint of the generating binary.
- [ ] A documented runnable generator reproduces the fixture deterministically.
- [ ] A fast assertion fails when the installed Pandoc version differs from fixture metadata.
- [ ] Mutating production output format to `plain` makes the independent byte-equivalence oracle RED.
- [ ] Corpus cardinality/order and all timeout/group-reap hardening tests remain covered.
- [ ] Paired timing quantifies eliminated subprocesses and runner time.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
